instructions: Put the rice and 2 cups of water in a pot and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered.
In a bowl, whisk the tapioca starch, tempura flour, salt, white pepper and Golden Mountain sauce. Slowly whisk in 1 cup of ice-cold water until smooth. Let the batter rest for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, thaw the mussel meat if it's frozen and pat it dry. Thinly slice the green onions and chop 1/4 cup of cilantro. Rinse the bean sprouts and drain them well.
Stir the mussel meat into the batter.
Heat 4 tablespoons of the oil in a 10 or 12 inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. Pour in half the batter and mussels.
Right away, crack 2 eggs over the batter and break the yolks with a fork so they spread. Scatter half the green onions and cilantro on top.

Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is golden and the batter has set. Flip it and cook the other side for 2 minutes. Keep flipping until both sides are golden and crisp. Transfer it to a plate.
Add the remaining 4 tablespoons of oil to the pan and make the second pancake the same way with the rest of the batter, eggs, green onions and cilantro.
Stir-fry the bean sprouts in the same pan over high heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until they soften but still crunch.
Pile the bean sprouts on a platter and top with the pancakes, cut into wedges. Serve with the rice and the sweet chili sauce in a small bowl.
method_notes: Only two close versions could be read, from Hungry in Thailand and Cup of Yum, and they share one recipe (5 from 1 and 5 from 2 ratings). The batter is tapioca starch and tempura flour whisked with ice-cold water, with eggs cracked over the top and a pile of fried bean sprouts underneath. The source is written for 2, so it is doubled and cooked as two pancakes. The sources give no dip; sweet chili sauce is what other Hoy Tod pages serve, and rice is added to make it a dinner. Golden Mountain sauce contains soy and wheat.
